title: CIA MDR

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: CIA MDR
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

Mandatory Declassification Review request: withheld portions of five released STARGATE (CREST) documents, 1974-1976

Dear Information and Privacy Coordinator,

Under Section 3.5 of Executive Order 13526, I request mandatory declassification review of the withheld portions of the following documents, which the Agency has already released in its STARGATE collection (CREST). Each is identified by its CREST document number, so it can be located with little effort. To my knowledge none is the subject of pending litigation, and none has been reviewed for declassification in the past two years.

1. CIA-RDP79-00999A000300100011-9, OTS/CB memorandum of 21 January 1975, page 3, paragraph 7: the redacted name of the test "given ... by OTS/BAB" to P. Price and H. Hammid.

2. CIA-RDP79-00999A000400050001-5, "Paranormal Investigations: Outline of 'Basic' Research Tasks": on the first page, the redaction in the line "WAIS/PAS test (by ...)" and the withheld handwritten annotations; on the last page, the redactions in paragraph 9 of Part IV.

3. CIA-RDP79-00999A000400050006-0, OTS/BAB Memorandum 163-75, 29 April 1975: the two pages marked "Next 2 Page(s) In Document Exempt," and the redacted block following "Coordinates given Pat:" on page 2 of the memorandum for the record.

4. CIA-RDP96-00787R000700100003-3, SRI Proposal ISH 74-266, 20 December 1974: the page marked "PAGE(S) 7 MISSING," and the four pages marked "Next 4 Page(s) In Document Exempt" that precede Dr. H. E. Puthoff's letter of 12 July 1974.

5. CIA-RDP96-00787R000200120001-8, letter of 26 February 1976 from Dr. H. E. Puthoff: the redacted addressee block.

Basis. Items 1 through 4 date from 1974 and 1975 and are now more than 50 years old. Under Section 3.3(h) of Executive Order 13526, classified information that old is declassified unless its release should clearly and demonstrably be expected to reveal the identity of a confidential human source or a human intelligence source, or key design concepts of weapons of mass destruction, or unless it falls within an exemption approved under Section 3.3(h)(2). The name of a psychological test, the office that administered it, and the contents of a 1974 proposal for medical and psychological testing are none of these. The redactions in these documents were made when they were released between 2001 and 2003, well before the 50-year mark. Item 5 (February 1976) reaches 50 years on 31 December 2026; I ask that it be reviewed under the standard that applies on the date of review.

Where a personal name must remain withheld on another legal basis, I ask that the office or component be released in its place. If any portion remains classified, I ask that the response identify the specific exemption category relied on for each withheld portion, so that I can consider an appeal.

I am a researcher and author and will publish the results. Electronic copies, please.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Jerome McClure

title: CIA-Kress

communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

for 1 January 1973 through 31 December 1977. Items 1 through 5 are cited by originator, subject and date in an Agency publication, Kenneth A. Kress, "Parapsychology in Intelligence: A Personal Review and Conclusions," Studies in Intelligence, Vol. 21, No. 4 (Winter 1977), released by the Agency as CIA-RDP96-00791R000200030040-0 ("Kress 1977").

1. Kress 1977, footnote 17: OTS/SDB, Notes on Interviews with F. P., E. L., C. J., K. G., and V. C., January 1975 (SECRET).

2. Kress 1977, footnote 18: DDO/NE, Memorandum for OTS/BAB, Subject: Experimental Collection Activity Relating to Libya, 8 October 1975 (SECRET), with its attachments.

3. Kress 1977, footnote 16:
   a. Chief/Division D/DDO, Memorandum for C/D&E, Subject: Perceptual Augmentation Techniques, 24 January 1975;
   b. AC/SE/DDO, Memorandum for C/D&E, Subject: Perceptual Augmentation Testing, 14 January 1975;
   c. C/EA/DDO, Memorandum for Director of Technical Service, Subject: Exploration of Operational Potential of "Paranormals", 5 February 1975;
   d. C/Libya/EL/NE/DDO, Memorandum for OTS/CB, Subject: Libyan Desk Requirement for Psychic Experiments Relating to Libya, 31 January 1975;
   e. CI/Staff/DDO, Memorandum for the Record, Subject: SRI Experiment, 12 December 1974.

4. Kress 1977, footnote 15: C/AOB/OTS, Memorandum for the Record, Subject: Parapsychology/"Remote Viewing", 20 April 1976 (printed as "S/AOB/OTS" in the 1999 reprint of the article, Journal of Scientific Exploration, Vol. 13, No. 1). Kress cites this memorandum for the operations officer's conclusion on Mr. Price's remote viewing of two foreign embassies, "It is my considered opinion that this technique ... offers definite operational possibilities." I also request any other written evaluation of that test by the operations officer, which Kress's 1999 Postscript describes as "a written, positive evaluation."

5. These records, also cited in Kress 1977, which I have not found in the Agency's STARGATE release:
   a. footnote 7: K. Green, LSD/OSI, Memorandum for the Record, Subject: Verification of Remote Viewing Experiments at Stanford Research Institute, 9 November 1973;
   b. footnote 10: S. L. Cianci, LSR/ORD, Memorandum for OTS/CB, Subject: Response to Requested Critique, SRI Random Stimulus Generator Results, 12 June 1975;
   c. footnote 12: W. T. Strand, C/ESO/IAS, Memorandum for Director, Office of Technical Service, Subject: Evaluation of Data on Semipalatinsk Unidentified R&D Facility No. 3, USSR, 20 August 1974.

6. Reports and evaluations of the "Operational tests which continued after SRI funding stopped," as described in OTS/CB Memorandum 76-86 of 4 May 1976 (CIA-RDP79-00999A000300100005-6), for 1975 through 1977, including the evaluation by the requesting area desk described as a "somewhat confusing, but nevertheless official, report" (September 1975) in the Agency's outline of its ESP research (CIA-RDP79-00999A000400050014-1).

7. The two attachments listed on OTS/CB Memorandum 76-86 ("CIA Visit Request" and "Attendees").

8. Records of the receipt, evaluation and disposition of two Stanford Research Institute proposals, including any reply to Dr. H. E. Puthoff:
   a. Proposal ISH 74-266, "Technical Services," 20 December 1974 (CIA-RDP96-00787R000700100003-3);
   b. Proposal ISH 76-68, "Detection of Remote Low-Level EM Sources," 1 March 1976 (CIA-RDP96-00787R000200120002-7), with its cover letter of 26 February 1976 (CIA-RDP96-00787R000200120001-8).

Search. The Directorate of Operations memoranda in items 2 and 3 were addressed to Office of Technical Service components (OTS/BAB, OTS/CB and the Director of Technical Service, among others), and all of items 1 through 5 were available to the author of an Agency journal article in 1977. Copies therefore exist outside the originating Directorate of Operations files. Under 50 U.S.C. 3141(d), information disseminated from operational files into non-exempt files remains subject to search and review, even if the originating file is exempt. I ask that those locations be searched: the Office of Technical Service (including OTS/SDB, OTS/CB, OTS/BAB and OTS/AOB), the Office of Research and Development, and the files from which the Agency released its STARGATE collection in 2000 to 2004.

Retired records. In July 1986 the Office of Research and Development told SRI International that the primary data from the Price experiments (transcripts, drawings and audio tapes) were no longer available to the writer, that he could not determine "if these data were destroyed or if they reside somewhere in archives," and that he was declining further efforts to locate them (CIA-RDP96-00787R000200020041-5; see also CIA-RDP96-00787R000200020040-6). No search was made then. I ask that this search include retired and archived Office of Technical Service and Office of Research and Development records.

Privacy. I do not seek the names of individuals and accept their redaction.

Segregation. Please release all reasonably segregable non-exempt portions. If a record is withheld in full, please identify it and the exemption claimed.

Format and timing. I ask for electronic copies, and for interim releases as records are processed.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Jerome McClure

title: CIA BAB

communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

of the Technical Services Division and Office of Technical Service Behavioral Activities Branch (TSD/BAB, later OTS/BAB), for 1 August 1972 through 31 December 1977. Each item is tied to a document the Agency has already released in its STARGATE collection (CREST), cited by its CREST number.

1. Results, scoring and reports of the psychological testing that Agency personnel gave Stanford Research Institute (SRI) Project 3183 subjects in 1974, namely:
   a. the "W.A.I.S. (Client-administered)" and "In-depth interview" entries in SRI Progress Report No. 3, Table 4 (CIA-RDP96-00787R000200010007-4);
   b. the "WAIS/PAS test" listed in the Agency outline "Paranormal Investigations: Outline of 'Basic' Research Tasks" (CIA-RDP79-00999A000400050001-5);
   c. the "PAS testing" referred to in the Agency memorandum of 20 February 1974 (CIA-RDP96-00787R000200200024-4).

2. The "complete package of all these test results" prepared for BAB, as described in OTS/CB Memorandum 75-11 of 22 February 1975 (CIA-RDP96-00787R000200090003-0), and any BAB memorandum, analysis or report on that package.

3. The results, scoring and any report of the test that OTS/BAB gave two SRI subjects, P. Price and H. Hammid, described in paragraph 7 of the OTS/CB memorandum of 21 January 1975 (CIA-RDP79-00999A000300100011-9).

4. OTS/BAB memoranda assessing Mr. Patrick H. Price, 1974 and 1975, including the assessment on which OTS/BAB Memorandum 231-74 of 3 July 1974 (CIA-RDP79-00999A000400050005-1) relies.

5. From OTS/BAB Memorandum 163-75 of 29 April 1975 (CIA-RDP79-00999A000400050006-0):
   a. the materials given to Mr. Price on 26 April 1975, described as "the Personality checklist, an indirect assessment guide and a PRQ III" (blank copies of the versions then in use are sufficient), and any completed forms or reports Mr. Price returned using them;
   b. the "three cassettes" recording the 26 April 1975 interview, or any transcript of them.

6. TSD/BAB and OTS/BAB memoranda, 1972 through 1977, in the branch's numbered memorandum series, whose subject is ESP, parapsychology, remote viewing, SRI, or Mr. Price, and which are not already in CREST. For reference, the released memoranda in this series include 323-72 (2 August 1972, annotated "ESP file"; CIA-RDP79-00999A000400050011-4), 231-74, 163-75, 210-75 (CIA-RDP79-00999A000400050009-7), 65-76 (CIA-RDP96-00787R000200020003-7) and 287-77.

Privacy. Mr. Price died on 14 July 1975 in Las Vegas, Nevada. Ms. Hella Hammid was born in 1921 and died in 1992. I can provide proof of death on request. I do not seek the names or medical identifiers of any other individual and accept their redaction.

Relation to other requests. This request seeks OTS/BAB's psychological and assessment records. It is distinct from my request F-2026-01378, which concerns counterintelligence assessments.

Search. The Agency located and released related BAB and OTS memoranda from its files in 2000 to 2004 (the CREST STARGATE collection). To the extent responsive information was disseminated into files that are not exempt operational files, 50 U.S.C. 3141(d) requires that it be searched.

Segregation. Please release all reasonably segregable non-exempt portions. If a record is withheld in full, please identify it and the exemption claimed.

Format and timing. I ask for electronic copies, and for interim releases as records are processed rather than one release at the end.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Jerome McClure

Clarification on search locations (no change to the records requested): In July 1986 the Office of Research and Development wrote that it could not determine whether the primary data from the Price experiments (transcripts, drawings and audio tapes) "were destroyed or if they reside somewhere in archives," and declined to search (CIA-RDP96-00787R000200020041-5). I ask that the search for this request include retired and archived Office of Technical Service records. Thank you.

title: Nonprofit security grants

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: Nonprofit security grants
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

Documents sufficient to show, for each of federal fiscal years 2016 through 2026, the identity of each nonprofit organization selected to receive or that received a Nonprofit Security Grant Program (NSGP) award, and the dollar amount awarded to each — including awards under the NSGP–State (NSGP-S) and NSGP–Urban Area (NSGP-UA, formerly NSGP-UASI) streams and under the NSGP National Security Supplemental (NSGP-NSS).

Specifically, I request:

- Selected/recommended subrecipient lists. The list of nonprofit organizations recommended for funding that FEMA provides to the Secretary of Homeland Security for final approval, and the list of selected subrecipients that FEMA transmits to each State Administrative Agency (SAA) after award decisions are made.
- Grant system data. The corresponding subrecipient and award data in FEMA's grant management system — FEMA Grants Outcomes (FEMA GO) and any predecessor system, including ND Grants — together with any report, query, extract, or export from that system identifying nonprofit subrecipients and their award amounts.
- Subapplicant data. Subapplication and Investment Justification (IJ) data submitted by or on behalf of nonprofit subapplicants.
- Subaward reporting. Subaward data reported to FEMA under the Federal Funding Accountability and Transparency Act (FFATA) and 2 C.F.R. part 170.
- Award announcement lists. Any award rosters, award lists, or recipient lists prepared by FEMA or DHS in connection with NSGP award announcements for these fiscal years, including the recipient lists underlying the National Security Supplemental award announcements of June 2025 and August 19, 2025.

For each award, I request the following data elements to the extent they exist: subrecipient legal name; Employer Identification Number (EIN) and/or Unique Entity Identifier (UEI); address, city, and state of the funded site; the SAA/state or territory; the designated high-risk urban area (for NSGP-UA); the funding stream (NSGP-S, NSGP-UA, or NSGP-NSS); fiscal year; amount awarded (both per site and per organization); the Investment Justification or project identifier; whether the award was a first-time NSGP award; and the award or subaward date.

If these data are maintained in a database or other electronic system, I request that they be produced as a structured data export (e.g., CSV or Excel) containing the fields above, together with any data dictionary, field definitions, or codebook. If no single document contains all of the above, please produce each record that contains part of it.

I am seeking recipient-level records — one entry per nonprofit per award. Program-level appropriation figures and national or state allocation tables standing alone do not satisfy this request; what I seek is the recipient-level detail described above. If, for any fiscal year, records such as state or territory allocation tables (for example, the allocation tables published in GPD Information Bulletins) are the only responsive records in FEMA's possession, please so state expressly for that year and explain why no recipient-level records exist.

Please process each fiscal year independently, and do not delay or withhold the entire request because records for one year are unavailable. If FY2026 award decisions have not been made as of the date of your search, please so state and process the remaining years.

If any part of these documents are exempt from disclosure, please be sure to review and release all reasonably segregable nonexempt portions of responsive documents, as the FOIA requires.

I request that I be properly classified as a media requester. I am an assistant editor at Reason Magazine who has written numerous articles on topics of public interest, and I am requesting these documents in an editorial capacity. Please contact me if you have any questions about my media status.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

All contracts, agreements, licenses, subscriptions, task orders, delivery orders, memoranda of understanding (MOUs), memoranda of agreement (MOAs), letters of intent, data-sharing agreements, pilot or proof-of-concept agreements, statements of work, scopes of work, modifications, and other agreement documents between your agency and Anthropic PBC (including any subsidiary, affiliate, or successor entity), or its authorized resellers or cloud distributors acting on Anthropic's behalf (including, but not limited to, Amazon Web Services, Google Cloud, Palantir Technologies, and Deloitte), that were active or entered into at any time between January 1, 2023, and the date of your search.

These records include, but are not limited to, any agreements relating to Anthropic's Claude products, including Claude, Claude for Enterprise, and Claude for Government, including under GSA's OneGov initiative or GSA Multiple Award Schedule contracts, and any agreements for access to, deployment of, or evaluation of Anthropic's models or services.

For each responsive contract or agreement, I request all documents attached or incorporated by reference, including pricing schedules, usage terms, data protection or data retention terms, acceptable-use or safety restrictions, service-level agreements, security requirements, and any related option or renewal periods.

I also request all records of communications between agency personnel and representatives of Anthropic PBC or its authorized resellers concerning the negotiation, evaluation, pricing, or terms of any such agreement, in any format in which they exist, including email, text messages, and messages on messaging platforms.
